newsitem.title: USA: Reliance Bancorp adopts rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Reliance Bancorp adopts rights plan.

text.p: Reliance Bancorp Inc said Friday it has adopted a shareholder rights plan, declaring a dividend of one preferred-share purchase right for each outstanding share of the company's common stock.
Initially, each right will entitle stockholders to buy a 1/100th interest in a share of a new series of preferred stock of the company at an exercise price of $60.

The rights would be exercised only if an individual or group acquired 10 percent or more of the company's common stock, or made a tender offer that would result in it acquiring 10 percent or more of its common stock.
The rights dividend distribution will be payable to shareholders of record on October 3. The rights are to expire 10 years later, on October 3, 2006.
Reliance Bancorp is the holding company for Reliance Federal Savings Bank and has assets of $1.8 billion.
The company said it was taking the step to protect the interests of its stockholders in the event of a hostile takeover bid. It said the plan was not adopted in response to any specific pending bid.

If that were to occur, each right, unless redeemed by the board of directors at a price of $0.01 per right, would entitle its holder to purchase a number of shares of common stock with a market value equal to twice the exercise price of the right - or, at the company's option, 1/100th of a share of the new series of preferred stock, Reliance Bancorp said.
